newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes quiet, Brent barrels loom for April.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes quiet, Brent barrels loom for April.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices were taking an early holiday Thursday, with little activity seen ahead of the long Easter weekend.
Cash traders said the feature in the stalled market was talk about what may loom ahead for April.
"We're expecting Brent barrels to show (in the U.S. Gulf) in April, maybe," said one cash trader, noting the ambiguity of where shipments will actually land.
Traders said they continued to monitor Glencore and Phibro moves, as both companies are said to be loading large vessels for trans-Atlantic Brent shipments.
Sources said they tracked Phibro fixing a Ultra Large Crude Carrier, supposedly for end-April arrival in the U.S.
Brent-holders were not showing their hand yet, but current discussion put Brent bids at 80 cents under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Traders were also eyeing Brent shipments from BP for early May arrival in the U.S. Gulf.
"There sure seems to be enough Brent making its way," said another trader.
For the grades, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was talked steady at a 30-35 cts discount to the benchmark, with no deals.
West Texas Sour/Midland was heard traded at a $2.38 discount to the marker, and May Postings moved at $1.74, 1-3 cts weaker than Wednesday.
Outright crudes recovered lost momentum from the morning to peg gains of around 10 cts, putting the benchmark at $20.70-80 a barrel.
